records.title: Cycle detection nils out non-cyclic shared references (DAGs), losing data
records.body:
## Summary

The cycle detection added in #33 uses a single visited set for the whole conversion and never removes entries from it. As a result any object reached a second time is converted to `nil` — not just objects that are actually part of a cycle. Non-cyclic shared references (DAGs) silently lose data.

Verified on `main` (v0.21.0):

```ruby
require 'quickjs'

Quickjs.eval_code('const o = {a: 1}; [o, o]')
#=> [{"a"=>1}, nil]                     expected: [{"a"=>1}, {"a"=>1}]

Quickjs.eval_code('const o = {a: 1}; ({x: o, y: o})')
#=> {"x"=>{"a"=>1}, "y"=>nil}           expected: both branches populated

Quickjs.eval_code('const o = {a: 1}; [{o}, {o}]')
#=> [{"o"=>{"a"=>1}}, {"o"=>nil}]
```

It compounds with depth. A 20-level DAG where every node references the same child twice loses the entire right-hand side at every level:

```ruby
Quickjs.eval_code(<<~JS)
  let cur = {leaf: 1};
  for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) { cur = {l: cur, r: cur}; }
  cur
JS
#=> {"l"=>{"l"=>{...{"leaf"=>1}, "r"=>nil}, "r"=>nil}, "r"=>nil}
```

This is a regression: before #20 the `JSON.stringify` round-trip duplicated shared subtrees, which is the correct-if-wasteful behaviour. `JSON.stringify` only throws on genuine cycles.

## Cause

`to_rb_value_inner` (`ext/quickjsrb/quickjsrb.c`) creates `r_visited` lazily on the first object, marks the object's pointer, and passes the same hash down through `js_array_to_rb` / `js_plain_object_to_rb` / the `toJSON` path:

```c
VALUE r_visit_key = ULL2NUM((uintptr_t)JS_VALUE_GET_PTR(j_val));
if (RTEST(rb_hash_lookup(r_visited, r_visit_key)))
  return Qnil;
rb_hash_aset(r_visited, r_visit_key, Qtrue);
```

Nothing ever removes the key. So the set answers "have I ever seen this object?" when the question cycle detection needs to ask is "is this object an ancestor of the node I'm currently converting?".

## Impact

Shared subobjects are common in real JS values — a config object referenced from several places, shared nodes in a parsed tree, the same record appearing twice in a result set. Every occurrence after the first becomes `nil`, with no error and nothing in the log. A caller has no way to distinguish it from a genuine JS `null`.

## Possible fixes

1. **Make the visited set path-scoped.** Delete the key once the children of that object have been converted, so the set holds only the current ancestor chain. Minimal diff and it restores exactly the pre-#20 semantics: cycles → `nil`, shared subtrees → duplicated. All three exit paths (array, plain object, `toJSON` result) have to delete, which is the only fiddly part.

   Caveat: duplication is exponential on a deep DAG. The 20-level example above expands from 21 objects to ~2M Ruby hashes. That is what `JSON.stringify` did too, so it is not a new hazard, but it is a real one.

2. **Memoize instead: map object pointer → already-converted `VALUE`.** Return the memoized Ruby object on re-entry rather than `nil`. Fixes correctness *and* the exponential blowup, and mirrors the JS object graph faithfully.

   Trade-off: the same Ruby object is now aliased from several places, so mutating one branch of the result mutates the others. Cycles also need to keep returning `nil` (the memo entry doesn't exist yet while an ancestor is still being built), so this needs both structures — an in-progress ancestor set *and* a completed-conversion memo.

(1) is the smaller, more conservative fix and is a strict improvement over today. (2) is what I would actually want long-term, but the aliasing change deserves its own discussion, so it may be worth landing (1) first.

The existing regression tests from #33 (`circular plain object converts cycle entry to nil`, etc. in `test/quickjs_test.rb`) stay green under either fix — a true cycle is still an ancestor when it is reached again. Worth adding the DAG cases above alongside them.

Happy to send a PR for (1) if that direction sounds right.

records.title: security: make central dependency-review unavailability fail closed
records.body:
## Organization-wide security-gate defect

The central required workflow `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml` currently documents dependency review as a **HARD diff-scoped gate**, but deliberately converts GitHub dependency-review API `403`/`404` responses into a successful skip:

```text
Dependency review is unavailable for ${REPOSITORY}; skipping dependency-review hard gate.
```

The job then exits `0`, skips `actions/dependency-review-action`, and allows the bundled required **Security Scan** to conclude success.

This is not equivalent to a clean dependency review and creates a false-green supply-chain result.

## Exact downstream evidence

`ContextualWisdomLab/EgressWeave` is public. On EgressWeave PR #66 exact head `c038a9509d1a8eae8561cc9081e67e12bd373d42`, Security Scan run `31108241013`, dependency-review job `92638903658`, the exact comparison

`10d0c51daf2ad278d66f43be479df8cf6b08ba6d...c038a9509d1a8eae8561cc9081e67e12bd373d42`

returned HTTP `403`. The workflow emitted the skip warning, did not execute `actions/dependency-review-action`, and still concluded success. EgressWeave tracks the buyer-visible downstream blocker in ContextualWisdomLab/EgressWeave#76.

GitHub's current documentation states that dependency review and the dependency-review action are available for all public GitHub.com repositories when dependency graph is enabled. The dependency-review REST API may be used without authentication for public resources; with a fine-grained token, `Contents: read` is sufficient. Therefore a `403` on a public non-fork repository is not valid clean-review evidence and requires diagnosis rather than normalization to success.

## Current integration opportunity

Open PR #799 already changes this same central workflow and exact-head dependency-review checkout contracts from protected `main` `f070c504c1cb06891b800d7ab0cf6ac7d3cf8eae`. If #799's exact head remains suitable, prefer extending that PR test-first rather than opening a competing workflow PR. If #799 advances incompatibly, keep this as a separate bounded follow-up from then-current protected main.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add an immutable RED contract proving the current `403`/`404` success-skip path is forbidden.
- [ ] Preserve explicit exact head repository + exact head SHA checkout and exact `BASE_SHA...HEAD_SHA` comparison binding.
- [ ] A `200` support probe may proceed to the immutable-pinned `actions/dependency-review-action` hard gate.
- [ ] A `403`, `404`, malformed/empty HTTP status, transport failure, timeout, truncated response, unexpected status, or other inability to establish dependency-review support must **not** be reported as dependency-review `passed`.
- [ ] For public repositories, fail closed on dependency-review unavailability and emit an actionable error telling operators to verify repository dependency-graph/security configuration and GitHub service behavior.
- [ ] Do not guess a root cause from `403`; record repository visibility, exact base/head, and status without leaking credentials or response bodies that may contain sensitive detail.
- [ ] If support for private/internal repositories lacking GitHub Code Security is required, implement only an explicit organization-governed exception with documented compensating controls and an unmistakable `not-applicable` result. Do not infer N/A from `403`/`404` inside branch-controlled code.
- [ ] Preserve least privilege: `contents: read`, no repository/ref/package/release write, no OIDC, no model credential, no caller-controlled code under a privileged identity.
- [ ] Preserve immutable action pins and the independent OSV, Trivy, Scorecard, CodeQL/SAST/secret surfaces; do not make another scanner a semantic substitute for dependency review.
- [ ] Add/update beginner-readable doctoring with APA 7 primary GitHub references and one `[Unreleased]` Security entry; no release/version bump.
- [ ] Prove focused contracts and the complete central test/coverage/docstring/compile quality contract, then obtain exact-current-head Security Scan and all other required central checks/reviews plus qualifying independent non-author approval before merge.

## Trust boundary

This is a required-workflow control-plane fix. Do not add a branch-local publisher, `contents: write`, push/rebase/merge authority, workflow self-modification, `-X ours/theirs`, temporary write-capable repair workflow, or execution of model-modified source under a write credential. Any repair branch must remain exact-head bound and stale-head refusing.

## Primary references (APA 7th)

GitHub. (n.d.). *Dependency review*. GitHub Docs. Retrieved August 7, 2026, from https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/dependency-review

GitHub. (n.d.). *REST API endpoints for dependency review*. GitHub Docs. Retrieved August 7, 2026, from https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/rest/dependency-graph/dependency-review

GitHub. (n.d.). *Dependency graph*. GitHub Docs. Retrieved August 7, 2026, from https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/dependency-graph

## Related

- Downstream evidence: ContextualWisdomLab/EgressWeave#76
- Current overlapping central workflow PR: #799
- Prior dependency-snapshot/base-graph repair: merged PR #736

[build-timings] Build Performance Report — 2026-08-20
records.body:
## Build Summary

- **Total build time (clean, cold cache):** 3m 46s (226.6s active timeline in `--timings` report)
- **Compilation units:** 372
- **Max concurrency achieved:** ~5 (host has 4 vCPUs)
- **Compiler version:** rustc 1.97.1 (2026-07-14)

## Top 5 Slowest Compilation Units

| Crate | Build time | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `aws-lc-sys` v0.40.0 | 87.4s (build script) | C library compiled via cc; pulled in transitively by `jsonschema`'s default TLS feature |
| `libgit2-sys` v0.17.0+1.8.1 | 70.4s (build script) | Native libgit2 vendored build for `git2` (`https` feature) |
| `syn` v2.0.117 | 25.4s | proc-macro dependency, unblocks 15 downstream units — largest fan-out in the graph |
| `jsonschema` v0.46.4 | 22.2s | |
| `rustls` v0.23.37 (x2 builds) | 21.9s / 21.7s | Built twice (build-dep and normal-dep graph) |

Other notable slow units: `reqwest` 19.2s, `regex-automata` 17.0s/15.7s, `ring` 13.8s (build script).

## Dependency Analysis

- **Direct workspace dependencies:** ~21 (via `cargo tree --depth 1`)
- **Total compilation units:** 372 (full dependency graph incl. build/dev deps)
- **Duplicate crate versions found:**
  - `bitflags` v1.3.2 (via `lsp-types`/`tower-lsp`) and v2.11.0 (via `libaipm-engine-spec`)
  - `regex` v1.12.3 built multiple times across dev/build graphs; `regex-automata` compiled twice (main graph + dev-dep graph)
  - `semver` v1.0.27 built twice (once for `libaipm`, once transitively for `rustc_version`/`derive_more-impl`)
  - `thiserror`/`thiserror-impl` v1.0.69 (via `gherkin`, a dev-dependency) and v2.0.18 (workspace crates) coexist
  - `tower` v0.4.13 (via `tower-lsp`) and v0.5.3 (via `reqwest`/`tower-http`)

  These duplicates are mostly forced by third-party dev/test dependencies (`cucumber`, `gherkin`, `lsp-types`) pinned to older majors and are low-risk to unify further without upstream changes.

## Cargo Lint Findings

- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`: **clean, zero warnings** (all lint groups incl. `pedantic`, `cargo` pass).
- `cargo fmt --check`: not run as part of this analysis; no lint findings suggest reformatting is needed.
- Build-time-relevant config already in place and working well:
  - `[profile.dev.package."*"]` sets `opt-level = 1` for all third-party deps (better runtime perf for native/C deps like `libgit2-sys`, `ring`) while `libaipm`/`aipm` stay at `opt-level = 0` for fast iteration.
  - `debug = 1` (line-tables-only) and `split-debuginfo = "unpacked"` reduce link time on Linux.

## Recommendations

1. **[HIGH IMPACT] Trim `jsonschema`'s default features.** `jsonschema = "0.46"` pulls in `default = ["resolve-http", "resolve-file", "tls-aws-lc-rs"]`, which drags in `reqwest`, `rustls`, `aws-lc-rs`/`aws-lc-sys` (87s build script alone) and `hyper-rustls`. The crate is only used in `libaipm-engine-spec/build.rs` to validate a **local** JSON file against a **local**, ref-free meta-schema (`jsonschema::validator_for(&meta_schema)`) — no HTTP `$ref` resolution occurs. Verified via a local experiment: changing the workspace dependency to
   ```toml
   jsonschema = { version = "0.46", default-features = false, features = ["resolve-file"] }
   ```
   and rebuilding removed `reqwest`, `rustls` (both instances), `aws-lc-rs`, `aws-lc-sys`, and `hyper-rustls` from the dependency graph entirely, with `cargo test -p libaipm-engine-spec` still passing (`committed_schema_matches_schemars_export`, `data_file_round_trips_through_engine_api_schema_file`, `data_file_validates_against_committed_meta_schema` all green) and `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` staying clean. Expected to save roughly 100-130s of wall-clock time on a cold/clean build (removes the two single largest build-script costs: `aws-lc-sys` 87s and most of the `rustls`/`reqwest`/`jsonschema` chain ~85s combined, much of which currently runs serially near the end of the build due to dependency ordering). **Estimated impact: HIGH.**
2. **[MEDIUM] Consider whether `git2`'s `https` feature (which pulls in `libgit2-sys`'s vendored 70s build script) is required today.** `crates/aipm/src/main.rs` currently only has a stub comment referencing a future `GitRegistry (git2/reqwest)` implementation — git2 functionality doesn't appear to be exercised by any command yet. If HTTPS git operations aren't yet wired up, temporarily building `git2` with `default-features = false` (no `https`) until the feature lands would avoid compiling libgit2's vendored C sources on every clean build. **Estimated impact: MEDIUM** (only helps clean/CI builds; incremental builds are unaffected once cached).
3. **[LOW] Unify duplicate `bitflags`, `regex`/`regex-automata`, `semver`, `thiserror`, and `tower` versions where feasible.** Most duplication originates from third-party dev-dependencies (`cucumber`, `gherkin`, `lsp-types`) pinned to older majors and can't be resolved without upstream crate updates. Low priority since these are mostly small, cheap-to-build crates and duplication mainly affects binary size, not build time meaningfully.
4. **[LOW] `syn` v2.0.117 unblocks 15 downstream units** — it's already a shared/cached proc-macro dependency across the graph, so no action is needed here beyond noting it as the graph's single biggest fan-out node; any further speedup would require reducing proc-macro usage across dependencies, which isn't practical.

## Trend

No previous `build-timings` issues were found in the repository to compare against — this is the first recorded baseline report. Future runs should compare against this baseline: **3m 46s clean build, 372 units, max concurrency ~5**.

records.title: Optimize GitHub Actions with Dependency Caching
records.body:
# 🚀 Optimize GitHub Actions with Dependency Caching

## Overview

The current CI workflow installs project dependencies from scratch on every workflow run. This increases the overall execution time and results in unnecessary network usage.

GitHub Actions provides built-in dependency caching that can significantly reduce workflow execution time by restoring previously installed dependencies whenever the lockfile has not changed.

## Proposed Changes

- Add dependency caching for the package manager being used.
- Use the appropriate cache key based on the lockfile hash.
- Restore cache before installing dependencies.
- Save updated cache after successful installation.
- Ensure cache is automatically invalidated whenever dependency files change.

## Benefits

- Faster CI execution
- Reduced network bandwidth usage
- Lower GitHub Actions runtime
- Improved contributor experience
- More efficient and reliable workflows

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dependency cache is restored before installation.
- Cache is automatically updated when dependencies change.
- Workflow continues to function correctly on cache miss.
- Existing CI behavior remains unchanged apart from improved performance.

## Checklist

- [ ] Add dependency caching to the workflow
- [ ] Verify cache restoration
- [ ] Verify cache invalidation after dependency updates
- [ ] Ensure CI passes successfully

records.title: Planner post-compile BEM integration: execution-order renaming and issue stamping
records.body:
## Problem

The planner's compile step (`compiler.py`) emits issues named by their **planning structure** — `P{N}-A{M}-WP{K}` — which reflects the phase/assignment hierarchy used during plan elaboration. This numbering has no relationship to the actual **execution order** determined by the Build Execution Map (BEM). When the BEM groups issues into dependency-ordered dispatch groups, the P/A/WP IDs create confusion: `P3-A1-WP2` might execute before `P1-A2-WP1` if the dependency graph says so.

Today the BEM skill (`build-execution-map`) is invoked **separately** after issues already exist on GitHub, and its output (the `execution_map.json` with `groups[]`, `merge_order[]`, and `deferred_groups[]`) is consumed by the fleet dispatch layer via `load_execution_map()` — which extracts only `groups` and `deferred_groups`, not `merge_order` — but is never fed back into the issues themselves. The issues carry **frozen compile-time dependency metadata** (`Depends on: P2-A1-WP3`, `Depended on by: P1-A3-WP1`) that is accurate when written but never updated if the BEM later changes the execution grouping. They have nothing about their actual dispatch position, group membership, or immediate neighbors in the execution sequence.

## Proposal

Add a **post-compile BEM integration step** to the issue creation workflow:

### 1. Runs BEM after issue creation

The planner recipe currently terminates at `compile → done(stop)` — issue creation on GitHub is an **out-of-band step** not part of the planner recipe itself (the `done` message instructs: "Use compile output to create GitHub issues and milestones"). This BEM stamp step therefore belongs in a **downstream recipe or skill** that runs after issues have been created on GitHub from the compiled markdown files. It should invoke `build-execution-map` against the full set of created issue numbers. The BEM analyzes pairwise dependencies holistically (including cross-assessment against in-progress work) and returns the canonical execution map.

### 2. Renames/re-numbers issues to match BEM order

Write a post-BEM script or skill step that:

- Reads the BEM `execution_map.json` output — primarily `groups[]` (the actual dispatch structure consumed downstream) rather than `merge_order` (a derived flattened list not currently read by `load_execution_map()`)
- Assigns a sequential **dispatch number** to each issue based on its position in the BEM's group-ordered sequence (e.g., `[D-01]`, `[D-02]`, ...)
- Renames each GitHub issue title to prefix the planning ID with the dispatch number, so issue titles reflect execution order at a glance
- The original `P{N}-A{M}-WP{K}` ID remains visible in the title and body for traceability back to the plan structure

### 3. Stamps each issue body with execution context

After BEM ordering is determined, update each issue body (via `gh issue edit --body-file`) to include an **Execution Context** section containing:

- **Dispatch group**: Which BEM group this issue belongs to (e.g., "Group 2 of 5")
- **Group type**: `parallel` or `sequential`
- **Dispatch position**: Its overall position in the merge order (e.g., "Position 7 of 23")
- **Immediate predecessor**: The issue that must merge directly before this one (issue number + title), or "None — first in group" for group leaders
- **Immediate successor**: The issue that merges directly after this one (issue number + title), or "None — last in sequence" for tail issues
- **Group peers**: Other issues in the same parallel group (if `parallel: true`)
- **Gated by** (if deferred): The in-progress issue(s) blocking dispatch

This gives each issue a self-contained view of "where am I in the execution sequence and who are my neighbors" without needing to cross-reference the full execution map.

## Design Considerations

- **Pipeline placement**: This is a **new downstream recipe/skill**, not an extension of `planner.yaml`. The planner recipe ends at `compile → done(stop)` with issue creation happening out-of-band. The BEM stamp step runs after issues exist on GitHub and needs real issue numbers for cross-assessment against in-progress work.
- **Idempotency**: The stamping must be idempotent — re-running BEM and re-stamping should overwrite the Execution Context section cleanly, not append duplicates. Use a sentinel marker (e.g., `<!-- BEM-CONTEXT-START -->` / `<!-- BEM-CONTEXT-END -->`) to fence the section.
- **Renaming strategy**: A prefix like `[D-07]` prepended to the existing title preserves the original while adding order visibility. Must handle re-runs (strip old prefix before applying new one).
- **Branch name slug impact**: `_slugify()` in `execution/github.py` derives branch names from issue titles. A `[D-07]` prefix would produce branch names like `d-07-p3-a1-wp2-add-auth-module-1234`. Decision needed: either (a) strip `[D-NN]` prefixes in `_slugify` before branch computation, (b) store dispatch number as body metadata / label only and keep it out of titles, or (c) accept the prefix in branch names. Implementation must address this.
- **GitHub API discipline**: Per AGENTS.md, mutating API calls require 1-second delays between calls. For N issues, title rename + body stamp = up to 2N sequential REST calls (2N seconds minimum). Consider using batched GraphQL `updateIssue` mutations with aliases to combine title + body in a single call per issue and batch multiple issues per request (reducing from 2N REST calls to ceil(N/batch_size) GraphQL requests).
- **`compile_plan()` relationship**: The compiler writes `execution_order` based on topological sort of the internal dependency DAG (`_dag_ops.topological_sort`). The BEM's `groups[]` ordering becomes the canonical dispatch sequence downstream. The manifest should be updated to reflect BEM-derived ordering when available — this requires a separate post-BEM manifest rewrite step.
- **`load_execution_map()` gap**: The current BEM consumer (`_findings_rpc.py:load_execution_map`) extracts only `groups` and `deferred_groups` from BEM JS

records.title: epic(semantic-incremental): recompute only affected per-file semantic facts after edits
records.body:
## Status: active semantic-incrementality controller

Parser/source/edit prerequisites:

- #6701/#2327/#7045 — canonical parser and fresh-equivalence proof;
- #5005/#7302/#7304 — one immutable full-document source/content identity per generation;
- #7409 — the only authoritative sequential `DocumentEditTransaction` and old↔new provenance map;
- #7402 — full-document→parser-input projection and data-section/boundary classification;
- #7246/#7247 — document-owned parser predecessor and exact canonical worker operation;
- #7375/#7379 — accepted parser-generation ticket and generation-conditional effect sinks;
- #7075/#7071 — document instance/generation publication authority and deterministic barriers.

Delivery graph:

- #7303 — impact/scope/work contract;
- #7306 — deterministic full-analysis contribution graph;
- #7308 — incremental contribution update and typed fallback;
- #7309 — generation-owned LSP snapshot and document-symbol vertical.

Related producer/consumer consolidation:

- #4047 — one declaration inventory for legacy/canonical workspace projections;
- #4746 — canonical per-file project fact shards and model delta ingestion;
- #7277 — completion consumes generation-owned semantic/type facts;
- #7280 — type inference reuses canonical class/method-return facts;
- #7286/#7288 — generation-owned diagnostic analysis and exact-input result reuse;
- #4241 — cross-file semantic invalidation;
- #1373 — edit-to-current-answer and work-volume evidence.

## Problem

Per-file semantic analysis remains whole-file work after every changed document generation.

Current behavior has the essential shape:

```text
SymbolExtractor::extract(ast)
  → unconditional full AST visit

SemanticAnalyzer::analyze_with_source(ast, source)
  → full symbol extraction
  → full class/export/package/generated-member construction
  → full semantic token/hover analysis
```

Generation-owned memoization can reduce repeated work within one accepted generation, but it does not make the transition from generation N to N+1 incremental.

The missing product contract is:

> Given the exact predecessor and final parser snapshots, #7409 transaction/provenance, and #7402 parser-input/source-boundary classification, update only semantic facts whose source, scope, or dependencies changed; retain or range-rebase proven unaffected facts; fall back visibly whenever the affected closure cannot be proved.

No semantic consumer may reconstruct edits through whole-string diff, cumulative shift, parser changed-range guesses, or another private coordinate map.

## Objective

Create one canonical per-file incremental semantic pipeline:

```text
prior FileSemanticSnapshot
+ accepted final ParseSnapshot/full source/parser-input projection
+ exact #7409 DocumentEditTransaction and provenance
→ typed SemanticEditImpact
→ retain / exact-range-rebase / recompute contribution closure
→ immutable final FileSemanticSnapshot candidate
→ #7375 accepted parser-generation ticket
→ #7379 sink-conditional semantic/document-symbol/project-fact publication
```

Every admitted incremental semantic result is observationally equivalent to a fresh full semantic analysis of the exact final source. Full fallback is a correct explicit strategy. Similarity, cloning, range shifting, or a nonzero reuse count is not itself work avoided.

## Authority boundaries

### Per-file semantic analysis — this controller

Owns:

- scope and contribution identity within one file;
- consumption of #7409/#7402 source/edit impact evidence;
- retention, exact range rebasing, local contribution recomputation, and full fallback;
- generation-owned per-file semantic snapshots;
- truthful semantic work receipts;
- exact fresh-full equivalence.

### Text/parser/source authority — existing owners

- #7409 owns final document bytes, sequential event application, and provenance.
- #7402 owns executable parser-input/data-section boundaries.
- #7001/#7375 own accepted parser snapshot/source/configuration identity.
- Semantic analysis cannot reinterpret these subjects or publish before the parser ticket exists.

### Cross-file/project invalidation — existing owners

#4241, #4746, #5241, and compiler-world owners decide which other files/modules become stale when public/project/compiler facts change. This controller emits changed per-file fact/interface categories; it does not create another reverse-dependency graph.

### Declaration/project fact projection — existing owners

#4047 owns one declaration inventory for legacy/canonical workspace views. #4746 owns durable project facts and per-file shard ingestion. Semantic contributions feed those authorities rather than becoming a second project model.

### Provider reuse — existing owners

#7277/#7280/#7286/#7288 and later providers consume the accepted `FileSemanticSnapshot`. They do not maintain separate URI/content semantic caches, rescan the AST, or reconstruct edit maps.

## Delivery graph

| Order | Issue | One-PR result |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | #7303 | Define semantic impact classes, stable scope identity, fact-family invalidation, exact provenance/range-rebase rules, and work receipts. |
| 2 | #7306 | Refactor full analysis into deterministic immutable scope/file contributions and materialized views with parity. |
| 3 | #7308 | Implement no-change, exact-rebase, and bounded local-scope recomputation with typed full fallback and fresh-full equivalence. |
| 4 | #7309 | Attach semantic output to the accepted parser ticket, migrate document-symbol/project-fact publication, and prove lifecycle/currentness. |

Do not implement #7308 by mutating the monolithic `SymbolTable` before #7306 establishes complete contribution ownership.

## Governing impact model

#7303 distinguishes at least:

```text
NoSemanticChange
RangeShiftOnly
LocalPayloadChange
ScopeBodyChange
ScopeHeaderOrBindingChange
ScopeTopologyChange
PackageOrFileContextChange
ImportPragmaPrototypeOrFeatureChange
ClassInheritanceOrGeneratedMemberChange
QuoteHeredocSourceBoundaryOrReco
